newsitem.title: USA: Pennsylvania retail wheeling plans due March 1.
newsitem.headline: Pennsylvania retail wheeling plans due March 1.

text.p: Pennsylvania electric utilities must file a pilot plan for competitive electricity sales with the state Public Utility Commission by March 1, the commission said.

This is part of the guidelines the commission adopted Thursday to implement the Electricity Generation Customer Choice and Competition Act, which was signed into law by Governor Tom Ridge on December three.
The commission said it also issued tentative orders calling for the state's electric utilities to file restructuring plans between April 1 and September 30.

In other actions Thursday, the Pennsylvania regulators issued guidelines for filing qualified rate order applications seeking authority to refinance with bonds expenses incurred as part of the restructuring.
The commission also said it adopted interim procedures to be used for the licensing of electricity generators.

These actions apply to the state's electric utilities, operating units of GPU Inc, PP&L Resources Inc, PECO Energy Co, Allegheny Power System Inc, DQE Inc, Ohio Edison Co, UGI Corp and Orange and Rockland Utilities Inc.
The competition law requires participation in the pilots by customers representing five percent of a utility's peak load for each customer class, the commission noted.

It said the pilot programs are expected to give the utilities, alternate electricity suppliers, customers and the commission some familiarity with the operation and possible problems of the competitive energy market.

Thursday's final order was based on comments received after the commission proposed guidelines in a tentative order issued December 12, its statement said. Comments on the final orders are due by January 31.
The commission said the restructuring plans will "unbundle" rates to show separate costs for generation, distribution, transmission and other service elements.
The plans will also list the amounts of stranded costs the utilities are seeking to recover through a competitive transition charge. ((-- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.))
